page: The Vultr vcg-a40-96c-480g-192vram is a bare-metal server configuration based on the Intel Xeon 6342 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the machine supplies 48 physical cores and 96 dedicated vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz with two threads per core. Memory capacity is provisioned at 480.0 GB of RAM, yielding 5.0 GB per physical core. Local non-volatile storage is integrated directly via a 1400 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by one public IPv4 address. While indexed within the Dedicated Metal GPU family, the instance configuration registers zero active GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight strong parallel throughput across multi-core and memory-heavy operations. The system registered 87,083.58 on stress-ng multi-core testing and 415.57 GB/sec on multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, placing both metrics in the top 25%. In-memory execution demonstrates high responsiveness, achieving 78.11 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and cached small-block memory bandwidth of 4,686.18 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core processing remains moderate, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the middle 50% at 1,762.79 alongside standard single-threaded gzip compression at 26.46 GB/sec.

From an operational cost perspective, the instance delivers high compute and memory density without the active overhead of GPU coprocessors. It exhibits tradeoffs common to dense multi-socket x86 platforms: uncached large-block memory read throughput (134.7 GB/sec) and write throughput (54.57 GB/sec) test at average levels, and CPU-based large language model inference declines steeply with model scale, yielding only 2.73 tokens per second on 70B parameter text generation. The configuration is best aligned with multi-threaded CPU workloads, large in-memory databases, caching tiers, ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency enterprise applications.
